title: P25-family depth-for-MLP reallocation at the 10M cap: eight Peri-LN blocks with a 2x MLP (d_ff 768) instead of six with a 3.33x MLP (d_ff 1280) at width 384 (9,566,208 params) on the 153-claude Lean incumbent
description: P25 family (depth instead of width; no exact backlog ID, nearest P24/P25): N_LAYER 6 -> 8 and D_FF 1280 -> 768 at unchanged width 384, 8 heads of 48 (4 ALiBi + 4 NoPE), MTP module, Muon/AdamW, schedule, init rule and token-budget batches, so the 10M cap is spent on two more sequential attention+MLP applications per token instead of MLP width. Depth is the strongest axis in the table (three untied wide blocks scored 477 vs ~650-687 for six at similar parameter counts, 144-fable vs 134/153), the MLP ratio is nearly free (124: 3x vs 4x neutral; 158: 2x at width 448 scored 676), and since 148 the recipe is capacity-limited rather than step-limited (val loss bottoms at 60-285 s), so the ~20% step cost measured by bench_pretrain (9.17 vs 11.53 steps/s over the first 60 s) should be repaid by a trunk that can chain more proof-state transformations before expert iteration; depth above 7 has never been run under the Lean protocol and never at the cap with token batches.
hypothesis: A proof step is a sequential computation: find the premises to cite (attention), apply the rule (MLP), repeat. With Peri-LN and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, each block is one lookup-then-transform; eight of them give every token two more rounds of retrieval and transformation than six, which matters most for the longer chains the RL metric scores (length >= 7 proofs are exactly the ones that need more intermediate proof-state features per token). The MLP at 2x (768) loses per-block transformation width, but 124 (3x vs 4x, neutral) and 158 (2x at width 448, 676 vs 687) say MLP width above 2x is close to free at this data size, whereas going from 3 to 6 blocks is worth ~+170 (144-fable 477 vs 134-fable 633 at the same parameters). The step cost (bench: -20% steps/s; predicted ~3,600 steps vs 4,540) lands the run at ~3.2 epochs, still past the 60-285 s val-loss minimum, so fewer steps should not bind as they did before token batches (146-claude). Risks: depth 7 lost -38 in 102 under the step-limited pre-148 regime and tied in 126 (7 blocks x 3x MLP at width 256: 633 vs 631); 11% slower RL sampling (bench 160 vs 179 samples/s) does not change the fixed-sample RL but lengthens the run (~1,900-2,100 s of 2,400); one-seed sd ~44 swamps small gains.
expected_delta: +5 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean; range -40..+40, one-seed sd ~44); keep needs > 687

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 153-claude except depth and MLP width; PeriLNBlock replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 768
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 153-claude: knob line N_LAYER, D, N_HEAD = 6, 384, 8 -> 8, 384, 8 and D_FF = 1280 -> 768 (8 patch lines, comment included). Everything derived is unchanged except what follows from those two numbers: 8 Peri-LN blocks each with fc1 (768,384)/fc2 (384,768); the MTP module's block also has d_ff 768; Muon shape scale sqrt(max(rows, cols) / 384): Q/K/V/proj/head 1, fc1/fc2 sqrt(768/384) = 1.41 (153: 1.83), MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); 768 != 3*384 = 1152, so muon_step's QKV-by-shape test still splits only qkv. Same slope table (4 ALiBi slopes 1/4..1/256 + 4 NoPE) in every one of the 8 blocks. Loss, optimizers, schedule, init rule, token batches (TOK_BUDGET 18,432) and handoff unchanged.
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,566,208 (bench_pretrain on an A40 reported 9,566,208 with fork 51604b3, vocab 107; by hand: per Peri-LN block 1,185,408 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 295,680 + fc2 295,296 + 4 LayerNorms 3,072; x8 = 9,483,264; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768). MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff as since 136-fable): 1,481,856 = 2 LayerNorms 1,536 + proj 294,912 + one block 1,185,408; pretraining trains 11,048,064 in total; the harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.57M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 8, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 768), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged code (caches[0] holds key positions; one cache dict per block, 8 now); no local fork checkout in this session, so the cached-vs-full equivalence check is the one 153 recorded (max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 at width 384) plus bench_pretrain's sampling run (4,096 samples, sample_acc 0.0315 after 60 s of training, no errors)

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 153)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (768,384) and fc2 (384,768) sqrt(768/384) = 1.41 (153: 1.83), head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 8 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 38 Muon matrices (153: 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (768,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 33 model Muon matrices (32 trunk + head) including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 32 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 38 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,566,208

batch.padding: to max len in batch (the batch's last, longest record); mean padded tokens per step ~18.3k of which ~18.3k real (>99% fill), vs the incumbent's ~51-54k padded slots for ~17.3k real tokens
batch.change: fairseq-style max-tokens batching replaces fixed 128 random records per step: per epoch, randperm the training records (GPU generator, seed), stable-argsort by total length so equal lengths stay shuffled, cut greedily into consecutive runs with count * max_len <= 18,432, then shuffle the run order with random.Random(seed). Loss is the same per-token mean over the batch's proof tokens; the shift augmentation, Muon/AdamW updates, warmup, clip and wall-clock cosine are unchanged. The val slice still uses fixed chunks of 128.
batch.size_note: variable: a run of length-sorted records with count * padded_length <= TOK_BUDGET = 18,432 tokens (128 x 144); on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 33..921 records per batch, mean ~136, so ~1,130 batches per epoch (incumbent: 128 fixed, ~1,204 per epoch)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq; same vectorised shift as abs over the n1..n64 name tokens)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch, then length-homogeneous batches in shuffled order (data-order change: within a step all records have similar total length; across steps lengths are interleaved at random)

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151/153: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 553 steps in 60.3 s = 9.17 steps/s (153's shape: 11.53; 148-fable's: 13.2), peak 9.27 GB, n_params 9,566,208, train loss 0.0725 / val 0.0885 at 60 s, sampling 160 samples/s (153: 179), sample_acc 0.0315

prediction: Metric 3-seed mean 692 (range 647-727); keep if > 687. Mechanism predictions: pretraining steps 3,300-3,900 per seed (central ~3,600 = 4,540 x 9.17/11.53 from bench_pretrain; 153: 4,540/4,479/4,489), falsified if the mean is < 3,100 (depth costs more than launch overhead) or > 4,200; epochs 2.9-3.5 (153: 3.97-4.01); final main val loss 0.076-0.092 and the val minimum reached later than 153's (165 s) because of the fewer steps; held-out greedy 0.955-0.975 (153: 0.9675); round-1 RL targets solved 700-800 (153: 766) and round-4 >= 1,100; RL sampling 190-230 samples/s in round 1 (153: 225; bench 160 vs 179); totals 1,850-2,150 s (153: 1,741), no timeout. n_params 9,566,208 (bench_pretrain reported the same), peak pretraining memory ~9.3 GB (bench).
